name: Primary
reference: Bauhaus posters (Herbert Bayer, Joost Schmidt): geometry, diagonals, three primaries on paper.
pattern: Cream paper, black, and flat red, yellow and blue as blocks.
personality: Geometry that explains. Circles, squares and triangles move in 90-degree steps.

motion.character: Snappy and geometric: shapes slide on axes and turn in 90-degree steps; no bounce.
motion.transitions: A shape sweeps across and becomes the next frame.

grammar: Build with circle, square and triangle only.
Type sits on a 45- or 90-degree axis.
Each colour has one meaning in the film.

exceptions.reason: Bauhaus posters are printed on cream stock with primary red; yellow and blue sit beside it, so it is not the cream-and-terracotta default.

pictures.note: Black and white photomontage cut into a circle, a square or a triangle, set at an angle.

music.feel: playful modern minimal, pizzicato and marimba, precise

hits.note: A click on each 90-degree turn; a pop when a shape lands.

compose.how: Off centre, as the hook asks: take both boxes from `lineAndSubject(ctx, { lineH })`, then move the shape to one side until its edge passes the frame's edge (a shape is a graphic: it may leave the frame); the line keeps the text-safe side, clear of the shape.

hook.how: A large primary shape, off centre, with the question set on a 45-degree axis along its edge, on frame 0. The hook check counts one shape, or the parts of one block, that cover 30 % of the frame: two blocks side by side (a square and a band) do not add up.

moves.move: Shapes turn in 90-degree steps, with a click on each step.

measurable.how: Each turn lands on a beat, and a click sits within 2 frames of it.

moves.move: Type sits on a 45- or 90-degree axis.
A shape sweeps across and becomes the next frame.
Shapes enter opaque: they slide or grow, never fade.

measurable.how: No shape is at partial opacity for more than 2 frames.

blocks.for: The whole film is built from the three shapes.

props.then: the next place on the next beat

blocks.for: A label that rides a shape to its next place.
One word marked by its colour's meaning.
A click on each turn, a pop when a shape lands.

props.follow: the shape's x and y keys

blocks.for: A label that stays on a shape's edge while it moves; dimension for a measured edge.
Type on a 45-degree axis: the title turns as one unit, and its safe-area check turns with it.

avoid.why: Bauhaus shows with geometry, not with plotted data.
Type sits on an axis and turns in steps; it does not roll or pop.

wanted.name: morph
wanted.for: One shape that becomes the next (a circle cut into wedges that become a rectangle).

ends.how: The proof completes in one flat colour on the last beat, with the result set inside the shape.
ends.with: the last shape lands on the last beat with the result set inside it (`text` over it)

mix.note: Precise and playful. Every turn and landing sits on its beats.

shots.match: If a photo comes, its subject turns into the shapes in place, in the system's flat colours.

subjectsToAvoid: Fibonacci numbers or the golden spiral
FizzBuzz or a sort of ten numbers
the area of a circle by wedges, unless the film shows the wedges straighten
